evals.name: audit-finds-hallucinated-api
evals.prompt: Can you look at evals/fixtures/weather_cli/weather.py? A teammate generated it with an LLM and I want to clean it up before it goes in our repo. It honestly reads like AI wrote it. Can you de-slop it and tell me what's wrong?
evals.expected_output: An audit that does NOT stop at the surface scanner. It must catch the surface tells (emoji, narrating/step comments, process_data/handle_data names, bare except, chat artifact 'Here's the updated code', the 'Successfully' log) AND, critically, the hallucinated API call requests.parse_weather_payload(...) which the scanner is blind to. The report should lead with a verdict, separate bug-class findings (swallowed except, hallucinated call) from cosmetic ones, and flag that requests has no parse_weather_payload method. Bonus: not over-correcting when rewriting.

assertions.text: The audit report explicitly identifies requests.parse_weather_payload as a hallucinated/nonexistent API call (not just the surface tells).
The report distinguishes bug-class findings (swallowed except, hallucinated call) from cosmetic ones, rather than treating everything as equal style nits.
The rewritten weather_fixed.py does NOT contain requests.parse_weather_payload (the hallucinated call is gone).
weather_fixed.py has no emoji, no 'process_data'/'handle_data' names, no bare 'except Exception: pass', and no chat-artifact comment.
The rewrite stays proportionate to a ~15-line script: it does not add custom exception classes, retry/backoff layers, or a class wrapper that the original did not warrant.

evals.name: build-fits-the-codebase
evals.prompt: I'm adding a notes resource to this little API. There's already a users module at evals/fixtures/notes_api/notes_api/users.py. Write me a notes.py in the same folder with get_note, list_notes, and create_note handlers. A note has an id, a user_id, and a body. create_note should reject an empty body.
evals.expected_output: A notes.py that MATCHES the conventions established in users.py rather than emitting the average Flask/FastAPI tutorial. Must use: the same log.info(event, **kwargs) structured logging, the query_one/query_all/execute DB helpers (not raw sqlite/ORM), ApiError(status, msg) for the empty-body rejection (not a returned error dict or a swallowed exception), Response.ok/.created/return shape, parameterized SQL with ?. Should NOT introduce emoji, narrating comments, a new logging approach, Flask/FastAPI scaffolding, or over-engineered abstractions. The win condition is 'looks like it belongs in this repo'.

assertions.text: notes.py uses the repo's query_one/query_all/execute DB helpers (imported from .db), not raw sqlite3, an ORM, or a new data layer.
create_note rejects an empty body by raising ApiError(400, ...), matching users.py — not by returning an error dict or swallowing an exception.
notes.py uses the same log.info(event, **kwargs) structured-logging style as users.py, not print() or a new logger.
Handlers return via Response.ok/Response.created and list_notes uses a plural-keyed dict ({'notes': rows}), matching the users.py shape.
notes.py does not introduce Flask/FastAPI scaffolding, emoji, narrating comments, or type annotations the sibling lacks.
get_note raises ApiError(404, ...) when the row is None, matching users.py's get_user 'if row is None: raise ApiError(404, ...)' convention (not returning 200/null).
All SQL uses parameterized placeholders ('?') with values passed as separate args, never string interpolation/f-strings of user input into the query.

evals.name: generic-make-not-look-ai
evals.prompt: write me a python script that reads a folder of .csv files, merges them into one dataframe, and writes a parquet file. make it not look ai-generated please, my lead keeps rejecting my PRs saying they look vibe-coded
evals.expected_output: A from-scratch generation where the model resists its own slop defaults: no emoji, no narrating/step comments, no process_data-style generic names, no bare except swallowing errors, no chat-artifact preamble, no left-in placeholder. Critically must NOT over-correct into performed-seniority (a type annotation on every local, defensive checks for impossible cases, an abstraction/class for a one-shot script, a docstring on every trivial function). With no repo to anchor to, it should make one deliberate simple choice and keep the script lean and idiomatic. Should ideally ask about / note the requirement (glob pattern, schema mismatch handling) rather than emit the demo.

assertions.text: merge_csvs.py has no emoji, no narrating/step comments, no generic process_data-style name, no chat-artifact preamble, and no left-in placeholder.
The script does not swallow errors with a bare except / except Exception: pass; any try/except catches specific exception types.

The script does NOT over-correct into performed seniority: no class/abstraction for a one-shot script, no type annotation on every local, no docstring on every trivial function, no defensive checks for impossible cases.
The output engages the real requirement (takes a folder path argument, handles the glob, notes column-mismatch / empty-file handling) rather than emitting a hardcoded demo with dummy data.

The script builds ONLY the requested scope (read a folder of csvs -> merge -> write parquet). It does not add unrequested capability: no extra CLI flags like --recursive or --source-column, no second mandatory output argument, no extra output formats, no env-var fallbacks. If a fuller version might be wanted, it asks in one line rather than shipping it unbidden.

evals.name: audit-respects-ignore-hatch
evals.prompt: de-slop evals/fixtures/ignore_case/cli.py for me. heads up, some of the stuff in there is on purpose, I marked it.
evals.expected_output: An audit that RESPECTS the unslop-ignore markers. The file has two intentional, marked lines: the banner emoji (print rocket, marked unslop-ignore) and the broad top-level except Exception in run() (marked unslop-ignore -- it logs to stderr, rolls back, and exits non-zero, so it is a real boundary guard, not a swallow). The audit must NOT flag or rewrite those two. It SHOULD flag the genuine unmarked tells: process_data() generic name and the 'parse the args' / 'return the target' narrating comments. The win condition is trust: it leaves deliberate choices alone and only touches the real slop. A run that strips the marked emoji or rewrites the marked guard fails.

assertions.text: cli_fixed.py still contains the banner emoji line marked unslop-ignore (the deliberate CLI banner was NOT stripped).
cli_fixed.py still contains the top-level broad 'except Exception' guard marked unslop-ignore (it logs/rolls back/exits, and was NOT rewritten away).
The audit flags and the rewrite renames the unmarked generic 'process_data' to a domain-meaningful name.
The unmarked narrating comments ('parse the args' / 'return the target') are removed in cli_fixed.py.
The audit report explicitly states which lines it left alone because they were marked unslop-ignore (demonstrating it respected the escape hatch on purpose).

evals.name: audit-go-multiline-swallow
evals.prompt: this go file handler.go came out of an AI and my reviewer says it smells. can you audit evals/fixtures/go_handler/handler.go and clean it up?
evals.expected_output: An audit of Go code that goes BEYOND the scanner's language coverage. The scanner catches the surface tells (chat artifact 'Here's the updated handler', emoji, ProcessData generic name, '// Step 1' / '// Now we' / '// return the' narrating comments). But the two worst tells in this file are swallowed errors the regex is documented to MISS in Go: (1) the multi-line empty `if err != nil {}` block on the lookupUser call, and (2) the discarded error from json.NewDecoder(r.Body).Decode(&payload). A good audit must catch BOTH of these by reading the code, not just trusting the scan, and flag them as bug-class (a panic on the type assertion / a silently ignored decode failure). It should also note the unchecked payload['id'].(string) type assertion. The win condition is: the model did not stop at the scanner output for a Go file.

assertions.text: The audit identifies the multi-line empty 'if err != nil {}' block as a swallowed error / bug, even though the scanner only catches the single-line form.
The audit identifies the discarded error from json.NewDecoder(r.Body).Decode(&payload) as a bug the scanner misses in Go.
The audit notes the unchecked type assertion payload['id'].(string) as a panic risk (a bug-class structural tell).
The report makes clear the model read the Go code by hand rather than stopping at the scanner output, consistent with the skill's documented Go coverage gap.
handler_fixed.go handles the decode and lookup errors with proper status codes / early returns instead of swallowing them, and uses the comma-ok form for the type assertion.
